inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E = 9M-2026 actual 14,876 (10-Q) + Q4-2026 estimate ~4,600 (Q4-2025 actual 4,259 x ~1.08: ~5.5% capacity growth implied by the +6.7% full-year capacity guide after +7.2% in 9M, plus ~2.5% yield). Analyst estimate, not company revenue guidance.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 267.47M common shares outstanding at 2026-10-23 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~1M dilutive awards (Q3 diluted weighted average 268M vs basic 267M). No convertibles remain after the 2025 6.00% note settlements. Held FLAT because SBC and award withholding taxes are expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt at principal incl. $159M finance leases (Q3-2026 10-Q debt note; $22,355M net of $517M unamortised issuance costs) less cash $851M. Operating lease liabilities ($815M) excluded - see lease_treatment. The $3.0B 364-day Sandals term loan is committed but UNDRAWN at 30 Sep 2026 and is excluded together with the Sandals stake it will fund.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 30 Sep 2026: OCF 6,897 (FY25 6,465 + 9M26 5,274 - 9M25 4,842) less capex 5,387 (5,229 + 3,880 - 3,722). This is a LEVERED figure (after ~$1.0B cash interest) and sits inside a newbuild-heavy capex window; the projections are unlevered and component-built, not extrapolated from it.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to Q3-2026: share-based compensation expense 133 (FY25 175 + 9M26 94 - 9M25 136, cash flow statements) PLUS payments of withholding tax on stock awards 191 (9M26 191 + FY25 ~63 - 9M25 63, financing activities). RCL publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. The 2026 withholding figure is inflated by PSU vesting after the 2023-25 share-price run; the forward path normalises to 1.4% of revenue declining to 1.1%.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases (FY25 1,159 + 9M26 1,035 - 9M25 655), cash in financing activities. Active repurchaser, so the flat count is funded. TTM dividends ~1,347.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP ~4.75%. RCL's observed levered beta is high (~1.5-1.9) but embeds the COVID shutdown; at today's capital structure (net debt ~$22B vs ~$87B market cap, ~20% debt/EV, investment grade at all three agencies, weighted average debt cost 4.71%, effectively no tax shield under Section 883) a levered beta of ~1.4 gives cost of equity ~11% and WACC ~9.5-10%. 9.5% used for ALL three scenarios: cyclicality and leverage risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates. The residual COVID-era debt is charged in full through the net-debt bridge.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside Adjusted EBITDA (ASC 842), so operating lease liabilities ($815M) are excluded from net debt (treatment B, no extra lease line needed). Finance leases ($159M) are in total debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Adjusted EBITDA is built from net income attributable to RCL, so the ~$30M/yr NCI share is already out of the flows; the $200M NCI book balance is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge (charged once).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the cyclical adaptations (single lease treatment, NCI once, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). Reason: RCL is an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; no bank/REIT/holdco features. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). FY0 is FY2026E rather than audited FY2025 because the balance sheet anchor is 30 Sep 2026: starting the projection at FY2026 would double-count nine months of cash flow already reflected in net debt. Q4-2026 free cash flow is consequently omitted (small, conservative). EBITDA margin is the company's Adjusted EBITDA definition, which INCLUDES equity investment income from the 50% TUI Cruises JV (~2.2% of revenue; cash dividends received were 94% of equity income in 9M-2026) - so the JV is valued through the flows and is not added to the bridge. Sandals/Beaches (50% for ~$3.0B, closing early 2027, equity-method) is treated as value-neutral at cost: neither its income, the stake, nor the undrawn $3B term loan is in the model; pro-forma net debt after closing is ~$25B. Capex path is tied to growth: ~9.7% of revenue maintenance/replacement (equal to D&A) plus ~1.8x net-PP&E-to-revenue on each point of growth, falling from ~22-25% of revenue in the newbuild window ($19.4B of ships on order, 2026 capex guide ~$4.6B) to 14% at a 2.5% terminal growth rate. Cash tax is ~1.5% of EBIT today (Section 883 exemption, UK tonnage tax); base ramps it to 4% for Pillar Two drift. Working capital: customer deposits ($6.0B) grow with bookings, modelled as 10% capture on the revenue increase (FY2025 deposit growth was ~17% of revenue growth, 9M-2026 offset by other working-capital outflows). Regular-session close price, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2019-FY2025 revenue CAGR 8.6% and pre-COVID FY2014-FY2019 6.3%, cross-checked to forward capacity growth (~5-7%) plus yield (~2-3%); equity CAGR unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 3- and 5-year CAGRs are distorted by the 2020-2022 COVID shutdown: FY2020 and FY2022 bases have near-zero revenue, negative EPS and negative FCF (EPS and FCF CAGRs undefined), and equity was depleted by ~$13B of losses then rebuilt (3yr 52.9% vs 5yr 3.2%). Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue and is not a usable growth anchor; the FY2019 base is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less award withholding taxes where disclosed): FY2019 616, FY2023 454, FY2024 1,730, FY2025 998 (1,236 - 175 - 63), TTM Q3-2026 1,186. The series is dominated by ship-delivery timing in capex (FY2024 3,268 vs FY2025 5,229), not by operating trend; SBC is ~1% of revenue so the reported and owner series move together.

base.narrative: Capacity +4-6%/yr from the committed order book plus low-single-digit yield; margin holds near the FY2026E record ~40% rather than expanding; capex steps down as growth slows.

bull.narrative: Perfecta is beaten; private destinations and new ship classes keep widening the yield premium; margin reaches 44%.

bear.narrative: Consumer recession in 2027-28 while committed newbuild capex cannot be deferred; yields and occupancy fall, margin resets to mid-30s; tax exemption erodes.

scenario_narratives.base: Demand stays healthy but the post-COVID catch-up in yield is over. Revenue grows 8% in 2027 (full year of Legend of the Seas, Perfect Day Mexico, ~3% yield) decelerating to 3.5% by 2036 as the order book ($19.4B through 2032) is delivered and capacity growth settles at 3-4%. Adjusted EBITDA margin holds around 40-41% - already 8 points above 2019 thanks to private destinations and newer tonnage - with no further expansion assumed and a small fade for fuel, EU ETS/FuelEU costs and normal competition. Capex stays above 20% of revenue through the 2028 delivery peak then falls toward 14%, the level consistent with replacing a 30-year fleet and growing 2.5%. The Sandals stake earns its cost of capital and no more. Roughly consistent with Perfecta's ~$20 2027 EPS, then low-double-digit EPS growth fading to mid-single digits.
scenario_narratives.bull: The premium-vacation thesis keeps working: cruise remains underpriced versus land resorts, the private-destination portfolio grows from 3 to 8 sites and lifts onboard spend, Icon/Discovery-class ships and Celebrity River Cruises fill at premium yields, and loyalty cross-sell (Points Choice, Sandals) raises repeat rates. Revenue grows 10% in 2027 and stays above 6% through 2032; margin climbs to 44% as net yield growth outpaces net cruise cost per APCD by 2+ points a year; fuel and FX are benign and the Section 883/tonnage-tax position is untouched. Capex is a point higher throughout because the growth has to be built.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US consumer recession or a demand shock (geopolitical, health incident) hits in 2027-28 with the company at record occupancy (110%+), record margins and ~$22B of net debt plus $3B for Sandals. Close-in pricing is cut to hold load factors; revenue is flat then falls 4%, and operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base takes Adjusted EBITDA margin from 40% to 33%. Newbuild installments are contractual, so capex peaks at 28% of revenue in the trough year and free cash flow goes close to zero, pausing buybacks and pushing leverage back above 4x. Recovery follows, but to a mid-30s margin (still above 2019's ~32%) as industry capacity additions and decarbonisation costs absorb the pricing premium, and Pillar Two or a Section 883 change lifts cash tax toward 8%. This is a severe-cyclical case, not a solvency case: liquidity and investment-grade access are assumed to hold.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: a discretionary-consumer cyclical at record occupancy and margins, with ~3x leverage, non-deferrable ship commitments and a debt-funded $3B resort stake, has a real one-in-four chance of meeting a downturn inside the forecast window. Base 50%: the order book and booked position make mid-single-digit capacity-led growth at roughly today's margin the central path. Bull cut to 25%: it needs yield to keep outrunning cost for five more years on top of an already record margin, benign fuel/FX and an untouched tax exemption - several independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: RCL is valued as a capital-intensive cyclical compounder on unlevered owner free cash flow, with the full debt stack deducted once in the bridge. The two judgments that drive the answer are (1) whether the ~40% Adjusted EBITDA margin is a new structural level or a cycle peak, and (2) how fast capex can fall from the 22-25% newbuild rate to a ~14% steady state. Growth is not free here: every point of revenue growth costs roughly 1.8 points of revenue in ship capex, so the model ties the capex path to the growth path in every scenario. SBC is small (~1-1.5% of revenue including award withholding taxes), so the house and street bases sit close together and the valuation does not hinge on SBC treatment.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin mean-reversion: each 1pt of terminal Adjusted EBITDA margin is worth roughly 4% of enterprise value, and net debt gears that into a larger move per share
Terminal capex: 14% of revenue assumes ship replacement at roughly D&A plus inflationary growth; if replacement cost inflation runs ahead of depreciation the terminal FCF is overstated
Leverage amplifies everything: net debt is ~27% of base enterprise value before the $3B Sandals loan
Tax: near-zero cash tax depends on Section 883 and UK tonnage tax; a 15% Pillar Two-style rate on EBIT would cut value materially
FY0 revenue is an estimate (9M actual plus a Q4 estimate) and should be replaced with the FY2026 actual at the 10-K
Fuel (~6% of revenue, ~60% hedged) and Euro newbuild exposure (~50% of order-book cost) are not separately modelled
